title: Making a dinosaur beat ’em up with Claude Code: the trick was dinosaurs that attack whoever hits them, poachers included
author: vinishkapoor
selftext:
Jawbrawl is a side-scrolling beat ’em up for the browser. Three friends fight poachers in a lost valley full of dinosaurs. Beat ’em ups look simple, but they fall apart fast if the depth movement, hitboxes and crowd fights aren’t right. I made it with Claude Code, working in small steps.

**Who made what:**

* **Code:** all written with Claude Code
* **Sprites, dinosaur models, backgrounds, music and sounds:** credited packs from OpenGameArt, Kenney, [poly.pizza](http://poly.pizza), Quaternius and Freesound, with every creator listed on the game page

**Workflow that worked:**

1. **One screen, one fighter, one punch.** Walking in 2.5D (up and down for depth) and a single punch hitbox came first, before any enemies.
2. **One poacher who walks in and takes hits.** Once that loop felt good, I added punch combos, jump kicks, running, dashing and grabs. Grabbing a poacher to knee him or throw him into his friends was the most fun to get right.
3. **Neutral dinosaurs.** Raptors and hornbacks graze until something hits them, then attack whoever is closest, poacher or hero. Describing it as one simple rule worked better than asking for “smart dinosaur AI”.
4. **Three fighters that feel different:** an all-rounder, a fast medic with long kicks, and a slow mechanic with heavy hits.
5. **Stages and bosses last.** A jungle river, a vine-covered city, a misty poacher camp and a volcano ridge, with a boss at the end of each. Those include a trapper with a harpoon gun, a tyrant rex and a major with a gatling gun.

Plus crate weapons (uzi, shotgun, pipe, machete), food for health, and keyboard, gamepad and touch controls.

[https://vinish.dev/jawbrawl-beat-em-up-browser-based-game](https://vinish.dev/jawbrawl-beat-em-up-browser-based-game)

If you’ve tried a beat ’em up with AI, what broke first for you, the depth movement or the crowd fights?

comments.author: thecrownforge
comments.body: The rule where dinosaurs attack whoever hit them sounds like it could create great fights. I’d watch what happens when a poacher and the player keep hitting one at the same time. If the target changes every second, the dinosaur may look random even when the code is consistent. Do you give it a short period before it can switch targets?
